# FDG4013

> DO NOT define public or protected internal constructors in abstract types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.4 Abstract Class Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG4013, CA1012
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Make the constructor of the abstract class '{0}' protected instead of protected internal

CA1012 reports a public constructor on an externally visible abstract type; FDG4013 reports the protected internal constructors that CA1012 does not (footnote 2). Changing a constructor's accessibility changes the public API: FDG4013 has no code fix, and CA1012's fix is breaking.

## From the book

Constructors should be public only if users will need to create instances of the type. Because you cannot create instances of an abstract type, an abstract type with a public constructor is incorrectly designed and misleading to the users.<sup>2</sup>

2. This also applies to protected internal constructors.

```csharp
// bad design
public abstract class Claim {
  public Claim() {
  }
}
// good design
public abstract class Claim {
  protected Claim() {
  }
}
```
